name: Science Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public scientific research data.

entries.title: CERN Open Data Portal
entries.description: Petabyte-scale open access to particle-physics datasets, software, and documentation from CERN's LHC experiments (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, LHCb, and others), released for research and education.

access.auth_note: Some derived research/analysis tools require a free CERN Open Data account; raw dataset browsing and download do not.

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: a capture it requested from Save Page Now.

coverage.spatial: global (international collaboration; hosted at CERN, Switzerland/France)

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (CERN Open Data Portal terms of use; software under its own licences, often GPL)
entries.notes:
Verified reachable this session (HTTP 200). Seeded as this vertical's first international (non-US) source per operator request to seed the new verticals international-first.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the terms of use (https://opendata.cern.ch/docs/terms-of-use) say "All metadata and datasets in the CERN Open Data Portal are made available under the terms of the CC0 waiver." Other content keeps its own licence; software is usually GPL. The earlier "dataset-dependent" caveat did not apply to datasets.

entries.title: Zenodo
entries.description: CERN's general-purpose open research repository, where researchers deposit datasets, software, papers and other outputs of any discipline and get a DOI for each. A primary home for research data and code that has no subject repository.

access.auth_note: Searching and downloading open records needs no account; depositing needs a free account, and the REST API uses a personal token for uploads.
access.rate_limit: Rate limited (HTTP 429 on excess); OAI-PMH shares the REST API's limits per developers.zenodo.org (exact figures not read)

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: a capture it requested from Save Page Now.

coverage.temporal: 2013-present (launch year from general knowledge, not checked)

entries.license: Metadata CC0-1.0 except email addresses (Zenodo policies); each deposited file under the licence its depositor chose
entries.attribution: Cite each record by its Zenodo DOI as the record page gives it; Zenodo, CERN
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The home page shows featured communities (EU Open Research Repository, AAS Journals and others) and a notice: "Scheduled maintenance: On Tuesday, November 3rd, Zenodo will be unavailable between 08:00 and 08:15 UTC for an infrastructure upgrade." An anonymous REST API call (https://zenodo.org/api/records?size=1) returned a total of 7611041 records, the newest created 2026-11-01; the OAI-PMH endpoint (https://zenodo.org/oai2d?verb=Identify) answered 200. The policies page says metadata is "exported in several standard formats such as MARCXML, Dublin Core, and DataCite Metadata Schema", and "Access to metadata and data files is provided over standard protocols such as HTTP and OAI-PMH". This entry catalogs the repository as a whole: its contents are deposited by third parties, so each record's own publisher is the depositor. Format lists the metadata exports only; deposited files come in any format. No bulk dump of the corpus was found.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: https://about.zenodo.org/policies/ says "Metadata access and reuse: Metadata is licensed under CC0, except for email addresses. All metadata is exported via OAI-PMH and can be harvested" and "Use and re-use is subject to the license under which the data objects were deposited." https://about.zenodo.org/terms/ says "Unless specified otherwise, Zenodo metadata may be freely reused under the CC0 waiver" and "Users of content ('Users') shall respect applicable license conditions." The operator is recorded as CERN per the terms ("hold CERN free and harmless"); an OpenAIRE role wasn't checked.

entries.title: Crossref Metadata (REST API and Public Data File)
entries.description: Metadata that Crossref members deposit for every Crossref DOI: bibliographic records for articles, books, preprints, datasets, grants and more, with references, funding, licence links, ORCID and ROR IDs, updates and retractions, and some abstracts. Open through a free REST API and an annual public data file.

access.auth_note: No sign-up for the REST API; a mailto parameter puts requests in the 'polite pool'. Monthly snapshots are for paid Metadata Plus subscribers; the annual public data file is free.

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 0).

coverage.temporal: every DOI registered with Crossref; 2026 public data file covers records up to part of March 2026

entries.license: No copyright restrictions on almost all metadata; some abstracts may be under publisher or author copyright (Crossref REST API documentation)
entries.attribution: Crossref metadata, via the Crossref REST API or the Crossref Public Data File (year)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The Metadata Retrieval page lists user interfaces, APIs (REST, XML, OAI-PMH, OpenURL, content negotiation) and bulk downloads: "We offer access to all of our metadata as bulk downloads for free... Annual public data file: Metadata for all Crossref content items in JSON format. Monthly snapshot: Metadata for all Crossref content items in JSON and XML formats, available to Metadata Plus subscribers." The public data file page (https://www.crossref.org/services/metadata-retrieval/public-data-file/) offers the "2026 Public data file": "this year the file weighs in at 208 GB and contains metadata for 180 million records, or all Crossref records registered up to and including part of March 2026", in JSON-lines .tar.gz. An anonymous call to https://api.crossref.org/works?rows=1 returned "total-results":188309402. Cadence daily refers to the API, which members update continuously (the blog says members register "around 37,000 records daily"); the public data file is annual. The XML formats belong to the XML API and Plus snapshots and weren't tested; rate limits weren't read.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the REST API documentation (https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/rest-api/) says "No sign-up is required to use the REST API, and almost none of the metadata is subject to copyright, and you may use it for any purpose. Some abstracts contained in the metadata may be subject to copyright by publishers or authors." No formal licence (such as CC0) for the metadata was found; the CC BY 4.0 in the site's page metadata (dc:rights) is for the web pages, not the data.

entries.title: ESA Gaia Archive
entries.description: The European Space Agency's archive of Gaia mission data: astrometry, photometry and spectroscopy for nearly two billion stars, with positions, parallaxes, proper motions, radial velocities and astrophysical parameters (Gaia DR3 and the Focused Product Release), queryable by ADQL over TAP.
entries.publisher: European Space Agency (ESA), with the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC)

access.auth_note: Anonymous ADQL queries work; a free Gaia user account adds private tables and longer-running jobs (not tested).

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 200).

coverage.temporal: Gaia DR3 (June 2022, 34 months of observations) and FPR (October 2023); DR4 announced for 2 December 2026

entries.license: CC-BY-NC-3.0-IGO (Gaia Data License, ESA Cosmos; commercial use governed by ESA's terms for space science archives)
entries.attribution: European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia, processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC); cite the data release per https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia-users/credits
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. Plain curl gets only a JavaScript loading page; headless Chromium renders it when it waits for DOMContentLoaded rather than network idle (network idle never settles, which explains the 60-second timeout reported on 2026-10-31). The rendered page reads "Welcome to the Gaia ESA Archive. Gaia is a European space mission providing astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of nearly 2000 million stars in the Milky Way", lists Gaia DR3, Gaia FPR and "Direct bulk download of Gaia data in ECSV format", and shows archive release v3.15.1. TAP checked: https://gea.esac.esa.int/tap-server/tap/availability answered "service is accepting queries", and an anonymous synchronous ADQL query (SELECT TOP 2 source_id, ra, dec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source, FORMAT=csv) returned two rows. The ESA release page (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia/release) lists DR3 (June 2022), FPR (10 October 2023) and "Gaia DR4 (based on 66 months of data) 2 December 2026". The votable and fits output formats are the usual TAP options and weren't tested; ecsv comes from the archive page; csv was tested.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia-users/license reads "GAIA DATA LICENSE Gaia data are distributed under the CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO license. For details and guidelines concerning commercial use of the Gaia data, please see the Terms and Conditions for the use of data in the ESA space science archives." That licence is non-commercial. Jurisdiction regional-bloc: ESA is a European intergovernmental agency (not an EU body), following how copernicus-era5-reanalysis is recorded. Science-almanac should set reachability.headless for this entry.

entries.title: NASA Earthdata
entries.description: NASA's gateway to Earth observation data from its Earth Science Data Systems program and Distributed Active Archive Centers — atmosphere, land, ocean, cryosphere, and more — with a common metadata catalog, search tools, and APIs.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Earth Science Data Systems (ESDS)

access.auth_note: Most data downloads require a free Earthdata Login account; catalog search does not.

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 0).

coverage.temporal: decades of satellite and airborne missions to present

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA data use guidance; unless a dataset is marked with a use restriction or license)
entries.attribution: NASA Earthdata; cite the specific dataset DOIs used
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The site lists DAACs (ASF, GES DISC, LP DAAC, NSIDC, ORNL, PO.DAAC, ...), APIs, the Common Metadata Repository, and Earthdata Login. NASA's Data Use and Citation Guidance (https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/engage/open-data-services-software-policies/data-use-guidance) states "Unless the content is marked with a use restriction or license, data provided from a NASA-led mission are licensed as Creative Commons Zero (CC0)". Some specific NASA datasets are already cataloged in climate-almanac (nasa-gistemp, nasa-grace-land-mascons); this entry is the gateway. Three things come from Earthdata's usual practice and weren't checked here: the Earthdata Login requirement, the formats, and the daily cadence.

entries.title: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.description: NASA's catalog of confirmed exoplanets and their host stars, plus mission data from Kepler, K2, TESS, and ground-based surveys, served through interactive tables, a TAP interface, an API, and bulk downloads.
entries.publisher: NASA Exoplanet Science Institute (NExScI), Caltech/IPAC, for NASA

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: a capture it requested from Save Page Now.

entries.license: unverified — no license stated; the archive asks for a standard acknowledgment in publications
entries.attribution: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with NASA under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page reports "6,451 Confirmed Planets" as of 10/15/2026 and lists a Table Access Protocol (TAP) interface, an API, and bulk data download. The acknowledgment page (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html) gives the standard acknowledgment text, used here as the attribution. It's operated by Caltech under NASA contract, so the jurisdiction is recorded as national (US). Several details come from the archive's usual practice, not from these pages: the weekly cadence and the votable/json formats. No license is stated, so none is claimed.

entries.title: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
entries.description: NASA's long-term archive of digital data from planetary science missions — Mars, Juno, Dawn, InSight, Artemis, and more — curated by discipline nodes and released to the public on a regular schedule.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Planetary Data System

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 0).

coverage.temporal: decades of planetary missions to present

entries.license: unverified — no PDS-wide licence; JPL-supplied material may be used for any purpose with credit (JPL Data and Documentation Use Policy, 2013)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page lists recent data releases, among them "Artemis II Mission Data" (October 7, 2026) and earlier Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Juno, Dawn, InSight, and Odyssey releases. The archive is built on the PDS4 (and legacy PDS3) standards. API availability comes from PDS's usual search services and wasn't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: PDS's citation page (https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/citing/) gives citation guidance only. The JPL Data and Documentation Use Policy for PDS (https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/jplcopyright.html, last updated 2013) says "Documents, images, videos, and data supplied to the Planetary Data System (PDS) by JPL may be used by any person for any purpose without prior permission", subject to a credit line, no warranty and no implied endorsement. It covers only JPL-supplied material, so the archive-wide licence stays unverified.

entries.title: NCBI GenBank
entries.description: The NIH genetic sequence database: an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences, part of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration with DDBJ and ENA, which exchange data daily.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine, National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI)

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 523).

entries.license: unverified — NCBI places no restrictions on use or distribution, but submitters may claim IP rights in their data; no licence is granted
entries.attribution: NCBI GenBank (International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes GenBank as "the NIH genetic sequence database, an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences" within the INSDC, whose three partners "exchange data on a daily basis". It says "A GenBank release occurs every two months and is available from the ftp site". The schema has no bimonthly cadence, so it's recorded as irregular. Not checked here: API access (NCBI E-utilities) and the 1982 start year.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: GenBank's about page (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/about/) says "NCBI places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the GenBank data. However, some submitters may claim patent, copyright, or other intellectual property rights in all or a portion of the data they have submitted." NCBI's policies (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/) add that there is no transfer of rights from submitters to NCBI; their public-domain sentence covers US Government web pages, not the sequences. So the licence stays unverified, and is never public domain.

entries.title: OpenAlex
entries.description: An open catalog of the global research system: scholarly works, authors, institutions, sources, publishers, funders and topics, linked by citations. Available through a REST API and as a free quarterly snapshot in a public S3 bucket.

access.auth_note: API works without a key but then shares a $0.10/day budget per IP address; a free account key gives $1/day of usage, with paid tiers above that. The snapshot is free to download.
access.rate_limit: Usage-priced: free key $1/day, keyless $0.10/day per IP (from the API's own notice and the pricing page)

coverage.temporal: all years indexed (start year not checked)

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (OpenAlex snapshot LICENSE.txt and pricing page)
entries.attribution: OpenAlex; cite Priem, J., Piwowar, H., & Orr, R. (2022). OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts. ArXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01833
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 for https://openalex.org/ (title "OpenAlex: The open catalog to the global research system"; the page is a JavaScript app). Other pages on openalex.org, such as /about, return 403 to scripts and headless Chromium with "Looks like you're a bot — please use our free API instead"; record pages are served to scripts per https://help.openalex.org/llms.txt. An anonymous API call (https://api.openalex.org/works?per_page=1) returned "count": 329080310 with the notice "No API key, so this request shares one free daily budget ($0.10) with everyone on your network's IP address. Get a free key with its own $1/day". The pricing page (https://help.openalex.org/access/pricing/) says "every account gets $1 of API usage per day for free", with pay-as-you-go and annual plans (Member $5,000/year and up). The snapshot release notes (https://openalex.s3.amazonaws.com/RELEASE_NOTES.txt) say "Public releases land on the second Wednesday of January, April, July and October (UTC)" and list RELEASE 2026-10-14 as the latest. The snapshot's other formats and the start year weren't checked. The publisher is recorded as OurResearch per the issue; ourresearch.org now redirects to openalex.org and the docs read didn't name the operating organisation, so that wasn't confirmed.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the snapshot bucket's https://openalex.s3.amazonaws.com/LICENSE.txt is the full text of "CC0 1.0 Universal", and the pricing page says "the data is a public good, released under a CC0 public-domain license with no 'personal use only' carve-out and no permission to ask". Cached full-text PDFs (a separate paid sync service) keep their own licences and aren't covered by this entry.

entries.title: ORCID Public Data File
entries.description: ORCID's annual snapshot of all public data in the ORCID Registry: researcher record summaries plus their public activities (works, employment, education, funding, peer review), in XML. The bulk counterpart to ORCID's public API, and the reference set of researcher identifiers.

coverage.temporal: annual files 2013 onward; latest seen is the 2025 file (snapshot as of 1 October 2025)

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (ORCID Public Data File 2025 record on ORCID's figshare)
entries.attribution: ORCID Public Data File (year), ORCID, Inc., with the file's DOI (2025 file https://doi.org/10.23640/07243.30375589.v1)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 to curl on the first request; repeat curl requests were then blocked by Cloudflare ("Sorry, you have been blocked"), and headless Chromium read the page. The page "Working with the Public Data File" links the annual files "2025 ORCID Public Data File" (https://doi.org/10.23640/07243.30375589.v1) back to 2020, and says "From 2018, the file is provided only in XML format" and that JSON can be made with the ORCID Conversion Library. The 2025 file's figshare record (https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/30375589, published 2025-10-20) holds ORCID_2025_10_summaries.tar.gz (about 46 GB) and eleven activities archives (about 16 to 19 GB each). No 2026 file was listed on 2026-11-01. The DOI prefix 10.23640 and orcid.figshare.com are ORCID's own figshare space, so this is the publisher's copy, not a mirror. ORCID's public API and its BigQuery copy aren't covered by this entry.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the 2025 file's record says "ORCID publishes this file once per year under a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication. This means that, to the extent possible under law, ORCID has waived all copyright and related or neighbouring rights to the Public Data File", and its licence field is CC0. The Public Data File Use Policy it points to (https://info.orcid.org/public-data-file-use-policy/) answered 429 with a Cloudflare challenge in headless Chromium, so that page wasn't read. ORCID needed a browser to answer after the first request; science-almanac may want reachability.headless for this entry.

entries.title: USGS Earthquake Catalog (ComCat) Event Web Service
entries.description: The USGS Advanced National Seismic System comprehensive earthquake catalog, queryable through an FDSN Event Web Service by time, location, magnitude, and more, with real-time GeoJSON feeds for recent events.
entries.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Earthquake Hazards Program

coverage.spatial: global (most complete for the United States)

entries.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes "an implementation of the FDSN Event Web Service Specification" for custom earthquake searches and recommends the Real-time GeoJSON Feeds for automated display. Two things come from the service's usual documentation, not this page: the output formats and the name ComCat. The catalog updates continuously; the schema has no continuous value, so cadence is recorded as daily.

entries.title: Protein Data Bank (wwPDB / RCSB PDB)
entries.description: The single global archive of experimentally determined 3D structures of proteins, nucleic acids, and complexes, managed by the Worldwide PDB partnership; RCSB PDB is its U.S. data center, providing search, download services, and web APIs.
entries.publisher: Worldwide Protein Data Bank (wwPDB); RCSB Protein Data Bank (U.S. data center)
entries.attribution: wwPDB / RCSB Protein Data Bank; users are encouraged to cite the original structure authors
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: rcsb.org returned HTTP 200, listing Download Coordinates and Experimental Data, File Download Services, and Web APIs. The wwPDB usage policy (https://www.wwpdb.org/about/usage-policies, HTTP 200) states "Data files contained in the PDB archive are available under the CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication" and encourages crediting the original authors. Three details come from the archive's usual description and weren't checked: the 1971 founding, the weekly release cadence, and the formats. The jurisdiction is international-ngo because wwPDB is an international consortium of data centres in the US, Europe, and Japan, not a treaty body.
